findings.title: Fix for F-2aa04fcb probably does not fix the E501 CI failure
findings.detail: Repository CI runs `ruff ... --select E501 --line-length 92 src`. The original failing line was 108 characters long: 11 characters of `    return ` plus a 97-character quoted literal. The fix only moves the literal onto its own line with 8 spaces of indentation, so that line is about 105 characters, which is still over 92. Ruff's E501 exemption for a single 'word' does not apply here because the string contains spaces. The harness lint gate reports a pass, but it may use a different configuration from the repository CI job that failed. If CI uses the same command again, it will probably fail on src/pricing/footer.py:3. The fix should split the literal into implicitly concatenated parts or add a `# noqa: E501`.

evidence.quote: "Orders placed before 2 pm on a working day leave our warehouse the same day by tracked courier."
E501 --line-length 92 src E501 Line too long (108 > 92) --> src/pricing/footer.py:2:93

findings.suggested_fix: Split the string into adjacent literals, each under 92 columns, so the returned value stays unchanged.

riskiest_assumptions: That the literal in footer.py matches the specified text exactly, character for character, with no hidden whitespace or non-ASCII look-alike characters. I can only see this in the rendered diff.
That the gate report's 'lint: pass' uses a different configuration from repository CI's `ruff --select E501 --line-length 92 src`. If they are the same, my E501 finding would be wrong.
That tests.test_footer imports the committed src/pricing/footer.py (package path set up correctly), not some other shipping_notice.
